titulo: Atlassian layoffs: about 1,600 jobs, $1.8B in buybacks
caption:
Atlassian layoffs: about 1,600 jobs, $1.8B in buybacks

Atlassian layoffs, March 2026: the CEO called it "the incredibly difficult decision". Here is the buyback column. (From the archive, not today's news.)

Atlassian, Mar 11, 2026 (CEO update to employees, 8-K): "I have made the incredibly difficult decision to reduce the size of our team"
In March 2026, Atlassian's CEO told employees, in an 8-K filing, it would cut about 10% of the team, about 1,600 employees. An 8-K is the report a public company files with the SEC when something material happens. Its fiscal 2026 10-K, the annual report, shows $1.8 billion spent buying back its own stock. A buyback is when a company uses cash to purchase its own shares.

Same fiscal year: $1.8 billion buying back its own stock, fiscal 2026. $1,800,485 thousand paid to repurchase Class A common stock in fiscal 2026, company-wide (cash flow statement, in thousands).
The math: $1.8 billion in buybacks (2026) ÷ about 1,600 job cuts = about $1.12 million in buybacks per job cut.
The facts: $1.8 billion buying back its own stock, fiscal 2026 (SEC EDGAR · Atlassian, Aug 14, 2026). about 1,600 jobs decided to cut (SEC EDGAR · Atlassian, Mar 11, 2026). The buyback is Atlassian's full fiscal 2026 figure, July 2025 to June 2026. The March 2026 update falls inside that year. The job count is about 1,600, the CEO's own figure.

Did Atlassian buy back stock the year it cut jobs? Per its own 10-K, yes: $1.8 billion in fiscal 2026. This shows two numbers from the same company and year. It does not say one caused the other.

Incredibly difficult. Here is the buyback column. (Our take.)

Send this to someone who got that update.

Synthetic voice. Sources: SEC EDGAR · Atlassian, Mar 11, 2026; SEC EDGAR · Atlassian, Aug 14, 2026.
